title: OSHA Bucket Truck Inspection Checklist (29 CFR 1910.67)
subtitle: For supervisors checking a bucket truck or other vehicle-mounted aerial lift on site before use and before travel.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
If an item fails, report it and keep the lift out of use until the defect is corrected; record what was done.
The manufacturer's instructions and site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Equipment, modifications and electrical tests
items: Records show a lift acquired on or after July 1, 1975 was designed and built to ANSI A92.2-1969, or an older lift meets it or was modified to conform
Any field modification has written certification from the manufacturer or an equivalent entity, such as a nationally recognized testing laboratory
Test record shows testing to ANSI A92.2-1969 Section 5, or a DC voltage test approved by the manufacturer or an equivalent entity
No alteration to the insulated portion that might reduce its insulating value
The vehicle provides a stable support for the aerial device

sections.title: Operator, controls and setup
items: The person operating the lift is trained
Lift controls were tested today before use and found in safe working condition
A boom platform designed mainly as a personnel carrier has both platform (upper) and lower controls
Upper controls are in or beside the platform, within easy reach of the operator
Lower controls override the upper controls
Each control is plainly marked as to its function
Outriggers in use sit on pads or a solid surface
On an incline, wheel chocks are installed before the lift is used

sections.title: Working from the basket
items: Each worker in the basket wears a fall arrest or restraint system that meets subpart I of part 1910
The system is connected at the boom or the basket
No worker is belted off to an adjacent pole, structure or equipment
Workers stay on the basket floor; nobody sits or climbs on the basket edge
No planks, ladders or other devices are used as a work position
No climbers are worn by anyone working from the lift
Boom and basket loads are within the manufacturer's specified limits
Lower controls are operated only with permission from the worker in the lift, unless there is an emergency

sections.title: Moving the truck
items: Truck is not moved with the boom elevated and workers in the basket, unless the equipment is specifically designed for it
Before travel, the boom or booms are inspected and properly cradled
Before travel, outriggers are in the stowed position
Aerial ladder secured (ladder and tower trucks)
Before highway travel, the aerial ladder is locked in the lower traveling position by the device above the cab and the manual device at the ladder base, or an equally effective means

references: 29 CFR 1910.67: Vehicle-mounted elevating and rotating work platforms
Work near overhead electric lines: 29 CFR 1910.333(c)(3), referenced in 1910.67(b)(4)
disclaimer: General guidance only, not legal advice. Check the current regulation and your employer's procedures.
